summary: Most common sustained arrhythmia: disorganized atrial electrical activity causing an irregular, often rapid ventricular rate. Risk rises with age, hypertension, heart failure, valvular disease, obesity, OSA; presents as palpitations, fatigue, dyspnea, or found incidentally on ECG. US prevalence ~10.55M adults (4.48%) (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline). Management runs two concurrent axes - stroke prevention (anticoagulate when estimated annual stroke/thromboembolic risk is >=2%, by CHA2DS2-VASc/ATRIA/GARFIELD-AF; DOAC preferred over warfarin except mitral stenosis or mechanical valve) and rate- or rhythm-control (early rhythm control favored for sinus maintenance; catheter ablation is 1L in selected symptomatic paroxysmal AF) - plus risk-factor modification.

news.what: Factor XI inhibitor asundexian failed in AF: phase 3 OCEANIC-AF stopped early for lack of efficacy - stroke/systemic embolism in 1.3% on asundexian vs. 0.4% on apixaban.
As of this date, no factor XI inhibitor is FDA-approved for AF; milvexian's LIBREXIA-AF phase 3 program continues.
FDA approved the FARAPULSE Pulsed Field Ablation System (first US PFA system) for pulmonary vein isolation in drug-refractory, symptomatic paroxysmal AF (ADVENT trial).
